messages.content: my sister door is closed. does that mean she is not home?
no. a closed door does not tell you whether she is inside or outside the house. you can ask or look for another detail without choosing the answer from the door alone.
make the grammar of my question better with the words we have.
the door to the room of my sister is closed. does that mean she is not home?
write a short story where a child asks before going in.

a child sees that the door to the room of his sister is closed. he calls her name and asks whether he can come in. she answers that she is reading and would like a little quiet. he says okay and leaves her to read. later, she comes out and asks if he still wants to show her his picture.
fix sister room and use no made up name.
a child sees that the door to the room of his sister is closed. he asks whether he can come in. she says she is reading and wants a little quiet. later, she comes out and asks about his picture.
does her need for quiet mean she never wants to see his picture?
no. the story says she asks about it later. she can want time alone now and time together later.
say it simply.
she can want quiet now and still want to see the picture later.
i asked my cousin if we could meet at three. they said at the library. did they say three works?
not clearly. they gave a place, but you still need to know whether three works. you can ask without changing the place.
write the question.
would three at the library work for you?
now they say yes, but i learn i cannot come until four. what should i say?
tell them the new information and ask about four: i am sorry, but i cannot come until four. would that still work at the library?
does the first yes mean four is okay too?
no. the yes was about three. a change to the hour needs another answer, unless you already know the other person is free then.
make a short message with no reason for the change, because i have not told you one.
i cannot come until four. would four at the library work for you?
what if i want to keep sorry?
i am sorry, but i cannot come until four. would four at the library work for you?
why not say i cannot leave work yet?
you did not give that reason. a clear message can say the new time without adding a reason you have not told me.
write a story about a child teaching a grandfather a game. do not make the child know everything or the grandfather know nothing.

a child brings a new game to the table and asks her grandfather to play. she knows how to start, so she gives him the first rule. he asks why one object must stay in the middle. she is not sure and looks at the game page with him. he reads a line she had not understood, and together they work out that part. she still helps him with the next move, while he helps her read the rule. neither has to know everything for them to learn together.
say that part simply.
he reads a line she had not understood, and they work out that part together.
use she had not understood in a simple sentence.
he reads a line she had not understood, and they work out that part together.
why is the grandfather useful even though the game is new to him?
he can read and ask questions. new information about the game and things he already knows can work together.
does the child stop helping after he reads one line?
no. she still helps him with another part. the story gives each person something to learn and something to share.
write a short line they can say when neither knows an answer.
let us look at the rule together before choosing.
write a short made up story that starts with i walked home. keep it simple.

i walked home with a book in my hands. the street was quiet, and i could hear music from a window. near the park, i saw someone looking at a map. i stopped to ask if they needed help, but they said they were waiting for a friend. i went on my way and thought about the story i wanted to read when i got home.
say my request simply.
write a short made up story that starts with i walked home.
does using i make it something you really did?
no. you asked for made up writing. i is the person telling that story, rather than a real memory from my life.
can you make it about the same person using she?

she walked home with a book in her hands. she heard music from a window and saw someone near the park looking at a map. she asked if they needed help. they said they were waiting for a friend, so she went on her way.
what did i ask you to change simply?
you asked me to use she for the person in the story instead of i.
did changing i to she change which road she walked?
no. it changed the way the person was written about. it did not give a new road.
someone asks if i want tea. i do, but i want to finish this page first. help me answer without saying i do not want tea at all.
thank you. i would like tea after i finish this page.
make my request simple.
help me say i want tea later, after i finish a page.
what if they ask whether i need them to wait before making it?
you can make the time clear: please do not wait for me if you want yours now. i can make mine after this page.
does that say i am making tea for everyone?
no. i can make mine is only about your own tea. you would need another sentence to say you will make it for the group.
write a sentence asking if i should make tea for the group when i am ready.
i can make tea for everyone after i finish this page, if you would like that.
say my last request simply.
write a sentence asking if i should make tea for everyone after reading.
if one person wants coffee, does that make the whole plan impossible?
no. you can ask what each person wants. they can have different drinks and still take a break together.
answer simply.
no. you can ask about both drinks and whether that works.
four people each bring one object for a game. does that mean four of the same object?
no. each brings one gives a number for each person, but not the kind of object. you need another rule if the objects must be the same.
make a simple example where all four bring different things.
one brings a cup, one a book, one a card, and one a toy. each person brought one object, and there are four objects together.
now the rule says bring one cup each. what changes?
then each of the four people should bring a cup. that makes four cups, rather than different objects.
say it simply.
then there should be four cups. the new rule chooses a cup for every person.
can one person bring two cups and another bring no cups while there are still four together?
yes, there could still be four together, but it would not follow the rule that each brings one. how many there are and what each person did are different details.
answer simply.
there could still be four cups together, but not every person brought one.
write a question asking about both details.
how many cups are there, and did each person bring one?
i put an old photo in my new room. the room does not feel like mine yet, but the photo helps a little.
something you already know can give you one place to start in a new room. what is in the photo?
the room does not feel like mine yet. the photo is of my family at a table.
then you have a picture of people and a place that you know, even while the new room still feels new. you do not have to make every part feel like home at once.
i want to write one sentence about that, without making it too big.
the room does not feel like mine yet, but the family photo helps.
can you keep family photo and say where i put it? it is on the desk.
the family photo on my desk helps, even though the room does not feel like mine yet.
does that say i hate the new room?
no. not feeling at home yet is different from saying you hate it. the sentence leaves room for your feeling to change with time.
what else can i put near the photo if i want only one more thing?
choose something you use or enjoy, such as a book, a drawing, or a small object with a memory. you can choose the thing yourself.
tell me a story where a child finds an old note saying meet at the library tomorrow and thinks it is a plan for the next day now.

a child finds a note inside a book. it says to meet at the library tomorrow. she asks her father what time they should go. he asks when the note was written. she does not know, but the book has been on the shelf for a long time. he says tomorrow is about the day after the note was written, not always the day after you find it. they look for more information before making a new plan.
explain that part simply.
tomorrow on an old note is about the day after it was written. finding the note today does not turn it into a new plan for tomorrow.
does that mean the note is false?
no. it may have been right when it was written. you need to know when to understand tomorrow.
answer simply.
no. the words need the time when the note was written.
write a new note that says we need to check the old plan.
check with my father before going to the library. the note i found is old.
say my request simply.
write a note saying we should check the plan because the old note may not be for now.
my aunt says she would love a visit but is busy this week. can both be true?
yes. she can want a visit and still be busy this week.
say it simply.
she can want time together and not have time for it this week.
what can i reply without asking her to choose a day right now?
i would like to see you too. we can talk about another time when you are less busy.
what if i am only in town this week?
then tell her that useful detail. she may still not have time, but she can answer knowing that you are only there this week.
write the message.
i am only in town this week, but i understand that you are busy. if there is no time for a visit, we can talk another way.
does that mean the aunt must change her work?
no. the message gives information and leaves her choice open. it does not make having a visit more important than everything else she needs to do.
can i ask about a short phone call instead?
yes. you could ask: would a short phone call work better this week?
use work in a short question.
would a short phone call work better this week?
two tools are in the same container. does that mean they do the same work?
no. two tools can be in the same container and help with different work.
say it simply.
no. the place you keep them does not say they do the same work.
write a short story where a child asks which tool to bring.

a child is helping her mother with a toy. she finds two tools in a container and asks which one is needed. her mother asks what part of the toy is wrong first. they look together, then choose the tool for that work. the other tool goes back in the container.
why ask what is wrong before choosing?
they need to know what work the toy needs. being in the container does not make every tool right for that work.
explain simply.
the problem helps them choose a tool. the container alone does not choose it.
does putting the other tool back mean it is broken?
no. it may work well for something else. not choosing it for this toy does not tell us that it cannot be useful.
my teacher asked a question and nobody answered right away. does that mean it was a wrong question?
no. people may need more time or more information. nobody answering yet does not make the question wrong.
say it simply.
no. a question can need more time or information before someone answers.
what could the teacher ask to help?
which part of the question is clear, and which part would you like me to explain?
i want a made up example with a question about cups.

the teacher asks how many cups were there before one was taken away. a child says they do not know the starting number. the teacher then says there were four. now the child can work out that three were left after one was taken.
what detail was not given at first in that example?
the starting number. without it, one taken away does not give a whole answer about how many are left.
answer simply.
the question did not give how many cups there were at first. that detail was needed.
can the teacher change the question after seeing the problem?
yes. adding a needed fact can make the question possible to answer.
picoboi, put these facts into a short sentence: i went to town, i saw my cousin, and i came home after lunch. do not say what we did together.
i went to town, saw my cousin, and came home after lunch.
say my request simply.
put those three facts into a short sentence without adding what we did together.
can you turn it into two sentences?
i went to town and saw my cousin. i came home after lunch.
what if i ask you to make it better to read?
i can change the writing or ask for another real detail. i should not add tea, a walk, or a story about your cousin as if you told me those things.
use better to read in a simple answer.
if you want it better to read, i can ask for another detail you want to use rather than making up what happened.
what question would you ask?
what is one detail about seeing your cousin that you would like in the writing?
i only saw my cousin across the street. we did not speak.
then i can keep that clear: i went to town and saw my cousin across the street, but we did not speak. i came home after lunch.
